text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A government lawyer accuses the opposition, seeking to stop parliamentary debate on the 1997/98 budget, of trying to paralyse the government by denying it money for the new financial year.
- A group of Moslem elders ask President Daniel arap Moi to pardon controversial Islamic preacher Khalid Balala and allow him to return to Kenya.
- Some 30 people have died of highland malaria in Nandi district in the Rift Valley, bringing the number of deaths to 50 in the past week.
- The chairman of the opposition National Democratic Party Raila Odinga says he is ready to work with rival opposition leader Michael Kijana Wamalwa.
- A Nairobi court is told warders in Nairobi's Industrial Area prison accept bribes to organise homosexual orgies for remand prisoners.
- The director of public prosecutions files fresh criminal charges against businessman Kamlesh Pattni and three top civil servants accused of stealing 5.8 billion shillings from the government.
- Embattled city mayor Dick Waweru preempts a bid to oust him after prematurely calling off a delegates' council meeting.
- Defections and resignations by members of parliament must be officially communicated in writing to the speaker of the National Assembly, he says.
- President Moi says the government will embark on a major rehabilitation and expansion exercise in government hospitals. ($1=54.50 Kenyan Shillings)
